The ASV supplies *the Lord* as the head noun of the article's own phrase, which it then completes with *of glory*. No other source token competes for that determiner slot — `κυρίου` is already spent on *of Lord* (rule 76) — so the article takes the supplied nominal with its determiner under rules 19 and 92, whose closing clause forbids handing a supplied determiner to a noun standing behind its own article. REV.11.15 is the exact-shape precedent and is unhedged: `τοῦ` → *the kingdom* of, where a genitive article governing its own expressed noun anaphorically supplies an italicized head noun repeating a lexeme from earlier in the same verse, and the unit heads on that supplied nominal. So the head is *Lord* and not *the*. Rule 22's *never the determiner* is what decides it, and it is not scoped to a substantival article: rule 60's closing clause says in terms that where the article supplies a nominal as well, rule 22 still chooses the head, `τῆς μελλούσης` → *that hour which* heading on *hour*. The corpus agrees at roughly sixty-five units to three, the three being JHN.21.17 twice, which cite no rule and read the other way at GAL.4.13 and 2CO.13.2, and 2CO.11.9, a rule 67 prepositional frame whose note concedes. JAS.1.11 corrected this very head from *the* to *man* in the preceding chapter, and JAS.1.25 repeats it. Two competing readings, both rejected. (i) Give the whole *the Lord of glory* to `δόξης` and leave the article `unrepresented`: refused by rule 92, the article standing before its noun. (ii) Mark *the Lord* `added` under rule 5 on the ground that no source token licenses a repetition of `κύριος`: refused by REV.11.15, which is this construction and is `aligned` on the article; rule 5's `added` resumptives in the corpus — 1PE.1.19 *even the blood*, JHN.1.9 *even the light* — are appositional phrases resuming a complete preceding phrase, not a head noun supplied inside an article's own phrase.

Genitive noun rendered *of glory*, headed on the noun under rule 17. The *of* sits here rather than riding with the article as in rule 21's *of the*, because the article's *the* determines the supplied *Lord* the ASV wrote in between and this *of* governs `δόξης` alone. REV.11.15 is the one exact-shape precedent and divides the boundary the other way, giving *the kingdom* of to the article and leaving `κυρίου` a bare *Lord*; that reading is defensible here and would make `δόξης` bare *glory*. It is one unit against one, so the seam is left where the verse pass put it and recorded here rather than re-derived.
Preposition realized by *with*; rule 36 keeps it on the preposition rather than reading *hold … with* as phrasal. Discontinuous from `ἔχετε` under rule 15.

One Greek noun rendered by the phrase *respect of persons*; *of persons* is the English idiom's own completion, not a second source token. Headed on *respect* under rules 66 and 91: the corpus spends that word on this lexeme, `ἀπροσωπολήμπτως` → *without respect of persons* heading on *respect* under rule 84. The competing head on *persons*, argued from the compound's `προσωπο-` element, is the decomposition rule 91 replaces with a query on the lemma.

The verse's one materially contested unit is s014. I give the supplied *the Lord* to the article and leave `δόξης` a bare *of glory*. Rule 21's sentence that an article carries nothing where the ASV gives its noun no determiner does not reach this case: the ASV did write a determiner inside the article's own English phrase, it simply determines the supplied head noun rather than *glory*, and rule 92 forbids handing that determiner to the noun standing behind its own article.

Head on *the* rather than *Lord* is the second contested decision inside s014. Rule 22's categorical *never the determiner* is scoped to a substantival article; here the article governs an expressed `δόξης`, so *Lord* is a supplied apposition rather than the article's substantival content, and rule 17's direct-realization test controls. A later chapter facing an article with a supplied head noun over an expressed genitive should read this note before assuming either way.

No `added` units. Every supplied English word (*My*, *the*, *Lord*) is licensed by a source token under rules 7, 11, 20 and 49; rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics on t012 and t013 as evidence rather than a verdict, and rule 86's test is not met since the article plainly stands.

Rule 67's own example `to euangelion` -> *as touching the gospel* is the same shape, and its warning against carrying a noun-headed reading across from a preposition carrier is why no head on a frame word is in question here.

The article's complement is the substantival adjective `πτωχόν`, so under rule 49 nothing else can carry the determiner and the supplied nominal *man* is the article's own as well: `τὸ τρίτον` → *the third part* gives *the … part* to the article and *third* to the adjective. Competing reading: give the article a bare *the* and *poor man* to the adjective on rule 17's generic-noun clause (*good thing* on *good*); declined under rule 66's closing clause, which holds rules 22, 49 and 58 untouched where the supplied word answers to an article. The corpus agrees: every unit finalized since rule 49 entered the contract reads this shape the article's way — twelve to none — and JAS.1.11's `ὁ πλούσιος` → *the rich man* is the same lexeme family in the preceding chapter, its head corrected from *the* to *man*. Article realized by the under rule 19.

Do-support auxiliary and lexical verb, discontinuous under rule 15; head on the lexical verb under rule 17. The clause is a yes/no question, so English requires do-support for subject-verb inversion whether or not a negator stands in it, which makes Do the inflected verb's own auxiliary under rule 9 rather than a word answering to οὐχ. The competing reading attaches Do to the negator on the ground that English negation also forces do-support; it remains defensible, but the interrogative inversion alone would have produced it.

Accusative object pronoun.

Anarthrous Greek noun, so the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the word it determines under rule 51's anarthrous clause, as JHN.19.13's *the judgment seat* has it, and no article competes for it. *Judgment seats* is the ASV's compound gloss of κριτήριον and no separate source token answers to either word. Rule 91's operational test decides the head and both candidate words are already spent in the corpus: the κρι- family heads on the *judgment*/*judge* word in all 67 of its units — `κρίσις` 23, `κρίμα` 8, `κρίνω` 36, none conceding — while *seat* is `βῆμα`'s own gloss at 2CO.5.10 and JHN.19.13, 2CO.5.10's note saying in terms that *seat* glosses βῆμα and *judgment* modifies it, and `θρόνος` takes *throne* in all 47 of its units. So *seats* is the supplied generic completion here and *judgment* is what realizes this lexeme, exactly as `σπουδή` → *earnest care* heads on *earnest* and `πραιτώριον` → *praetorian guard* on *praetorian* under rule 66. The competing head on *seats* is the accepted reading's, argued from κριτήριον denoting the tribunal rather than the act of judging; that is the denotational decomposition rule 99 names as the recurring failure and rule 91 replaces with a query on the lemma, and rule 66's `ζῷον` → *living creature* does not reach it, *creature* being a gloss of `ζῷον` where *seat* is another lexeme's.
